Excludes the 40 round-1 ids (ROUND1_IDS), the 240 ids in spot-check-round2/3/4/5-sample.json and X-IT-11.3.3 (ROUND6_EXCLUDE). No item text was changed by the spot-check. This file is the record of what was checked.

items.text: A manager asks for a new starter to get a laptop and email account next Monday. What kind of work is this?
items.correct: Service request
items.explanation: Providing something new that was planned is a service request, not a repair.

items.text: DIMM marking on the card says DDR5. Lab command?
items.correct: memory ddr5
items.explanation: The DIMM label says DDR5, and memory generation is typed with the memory command: memory ddr5. memory ddr4 names the other generation, whose key notch is in a different place so it would not even fit the slot; storage takes the drive interface (nvme or sata) and post takes the POST result, so neither accepts a memory type. See 2.4. Source: Course hw-board bench card (lesson 2.4 lab command list); JEDEC DDR4 and DDR5 DIMM standards (different key-notch positions).

items.text: A workstation with dual-channel capable board shows half the expected memory bandwidth in diagnostics after a upgrade. Two identical DDR5 modules were installed in slots 1 and 2. What is the best next action?
options: Update the chipset driver in Windows
Move them to the dual-channel slot pair
Replace both with a matched kit
items.correct: Move them to the dual-channel slot pair
items.explanation: Two modules in adjacent slots usually share one channel. The board manual names the dual-channel pair (often slots 2 and 4).

items.text: Allowed diskpart command in this block?
options: convert gpt on the OS disk without a ticket
items.correct: list disk
items.explanation: list disk only shows the disks and their numbers, so it changes nothing. clean, delete partition and an unticketed convert on the OS disk all destroy data; in this block you list, read and exit. See 3.1 / 2.6.

items.text: Incrementals ran Monday to Wednesday after Sunday’s full backup. What does a Wednesday restore need?
options: Sunday’s full and all three incrementals
Sunday’s full and Wednesday’s backup only
Monday’s incremental and the full backup
items.correct: Sunday’s full and all three incrementals
items.explanation: Each incremental holds changes since the previous backup, so all of them are applied in order after the full.

items.text: A PCIe riser was added; GPU artifacts appear. The riser is unpowered for a power-hungry card. Likely issue?
options: The wrong PCIe generation set in Windows
Not enough power through the unpowered riser
items.correct: Not enough power through the unpowered riser
items.explanation: A power-hungry card on an unpowered riser cannot draw enough slot power, causing artefacts and instability.

items.text: Which cable fault is most likely if a cable certifier reports split pairs?
options: Split pairs despite correct pin continuity
An open conductor on one pair
items.correct: Split pairs despite correct pin continuity
items.explanation: Split pairs: pins are connected correctly (continuity passes) but conductors from different twisted pairs are used together, so crosstalk fails certification.

items.text: A laptop charges only with the lid closed and shuts down when opened past 30 degrees. Which failure mode best matches?
options: A faulty AC adapter or barrel plug
The lid-close action in power settings
A damaged cable or connector in the hinge
items.correct: A damaged cable or connector in the hinge
items.explanation: A fault that follows the lid angle is mechanical flex: a damaged cable or connector routed through the hinge.

items.text: Work profile / MDM on a phone is:
options: Shop-managed enrollment you do not sidestep
Something you may remove to install an app
items.correct: Shop-managed enrollment you do not sidestep
items.explanation: A work profile or MDM enrolment puts the phone under the organisation’s policy: only the policy owner retires, wipes or changes it, so you do not sidestep it. It is not the user’s personal Apple ID or a personal backup app; those belong to the user. Removing it to install an app breaks compliance and removes company data, which is exactly the change you do not get to make. See 4.2. Source: Microsoft Learn, Intune device enrolment and compliance policies; Apple Platform Deployment guide (device management and User Enrollment).

items.text: What must happen before deleting files in the spool PRINTERS folder?
options: Restart the printer at its panel
items.correct: Stop the Print Spooler service
items.explanation: The spooler holds the files open; stop it, delete the queued jobs, then start it again.

items.text: Which IPv6 address is link-local and valid only on the local network segment?
items.correct: fe80::3aff:fe4d:12
items.explanation: Link-local IPv6 addresses come from fe80::/10; fd… is unique local and 2001:db8 is the documentation prefix.

items.text: You need to confirm a remote host accepts HTTPS only. Which test is most appropriate?
options: Connect to TCP 443 and check the certificate
Ping the host to see if it answers
Look up the host’s A record in DNS
Run tracert to the host to see the path
items.correct: Connect to TCP 443 and check the certificate
items.explanation: HTTPS is TCP 443; connecting to it and checking the certificate proves the service, while ping and DNS do not.

items.text: A server NIC team is in switch-dependent mode but the switch is not configured for that teaming. Symptom?
options: The server gets an APIPA address on the team
items.correct: Unstable or degraded link aggregation
items.explanation: Switch-dependent teaming (e.g., LACP) needs matching switch configuration; without it the aggregate is unstable or degraded.

items.text: Changing a shared AP admin password is:
options: Only a repair if the password was forgotten
items.correct: A change — shop process
items.explanation: A shared access point’s admin password affects everyone who manages that device, so changing it is a change: it goes through the shop’s change process and is recorded. Treating it as optional or as a silent repair leaves the next technician locked out with no record of who changed it. See 5.4 / 1.3.

items.text: Which hypervisor type runs directly on the hardware without a host OS?
items.correct: Type 1 (bare-metal)
items.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors (e.g., Hyper-V Server, ESXi) run on the hardware; Type 2 run as applications on a host OS.

items.text: Which of these is one of the NIST essential characteristics of cloud computing?
items.correct: Measured service
items.explanation: NIST lists on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service.

items.text: Guest shows no adapter or APIPA; host network is up. Next person?
options: The hypervisor owner (vNIC, port group, uplink)
The Windows Setup team, to reinstall the guest OS
items.correct: The hypervisor owner (vNIC, port group, uplink)
items.explanation: You ran the network checks inside the guest, the guest shows no adapter or an APIPA address and the host network is up, so the fault is in the virtual layer between them: a disconnected vNIC, the wrong port group or the host uplink. That belongs to the hypervisor owner. The printer vendor and “whoever has a screwdriver” have no access to it, and reinstalling the guest OS does not reconnect a virtual adapter. See 6.3. Source: Microsoft Learn, Hyper-V virtual switch and network adapter settings; VMware vSphere networking (port groups, uplinks); course 6.3.

items.text: You have confirmed a theory and applied a fix. What comes next in the troubleshooting method?
items.correct: Verify full functionality, then document
items.explanation: After implementing, verify the user’s outcome (and preventive measures), then document findings and actions.

items.text: Ping IP works, ping name fails. Domain?
items.correct: Name / DNS
items.explanation: Reaching the address proves routing works; failing by name points to name resolution (DNS). A display cable, RAID level or power fault would not let the IP ping succeed while the name fails. See 7.2 / 5.3.

items.text: Which closure note is most useful to the next technician?
options: Only the time spent and the user’s full name and desk
Cause, fix, how it was verified and any prevention
A thank-you message copied from the user
The word “fixed” and the closing date
items.correct: Cause, fix, how it was verified and any prevention
items.explanation: Cause, fix, verification and prevention let someone else understand and repeat the work.

items.text: You escalate a VPN ticket to the identity team. Which part of the package tells them what you changed on the PC and whether it is still changed?
items.correct: Current state
items.explanation: The escalation package has six parts: impact and priority, scope, evidence, actions → results, current state and the request. Current state is the part that says what you changed and whether it is still changed, so the owning team knows the starting point.

items.text: MEM beep, no video. Clean install?
items.correct: No. Memory domain first
items.explanation: Long beeps or a MEM code with no video is a POST memory fault, which happens before Windows loads, so reinstalling Windows cannot fix it. Check and reseat memory first. See 8.1 / 2.5.

items.text: The DHCP Client service is stopped. What symptom do you expect?
options: No lease: an APIPA address or failed renewals
DNS answers slowly, but every name still resolves
items.correct: No lease: an APIPA address or failed renewals
items.explanation: The DHCP Client service obtains and renews leases; when it is stopped the address fails to renew or falls back to APIPA.

items.text: In which order does Microsoft recommend running the system-file repair tools?
options: sfc /scannow first, then chkdsk /f /r on C:
chkdsk first, then DISM, then Startup Repair
Startup Repair first, then sfc in Safe Mode
items.correct: DISM /RestoreHealth first, then sfc /scannow
items.explanation: DISM repairs the component store that SFC uses as its source of good files.

items.text: A domain-level GPO and an OU-level GPO set the same option to different values. Neither is enforced and inheritance is not blocked. Which value applies?
options: The local policy, because it lives on the PC
The OU GPO, because it is applied later
The domain GPO, because it is higher in the tree
Whichever GPO was created most recently
items.correct: The OU GPO, because it is applied later
items.explanation: GPOs are processed local, site, domain, then OU (parent to child). Where two set the same option, the one applied later — the OU GPO — wins unless a GPO is enforced or inheritance is blocked. Creation date does not matter.

items.text: Which octal mode gives the owner read/write, the group read, and others no access?
items.explanation: Owner rw = 4+2 = 6, group r = 4, others 0: 640.

items.text: How do you start a Mac with Apple silicon in macOS Recovery?
options: Hold Command-R as soon as you hear the startup chime
Press F8 repeatedly while the Apple logo is showing
Hold the power button until startup options appear
Hold Shift and choose Restart from the Apple menu
items.correct: Hold the power button until startup options appear
items.explanation: Apple silicon Macs use the held power button and Options; Command-R applies to Intel Macs; F8 is a Windows habit.

items.text: A Linux user can reach a server but gets “permission denied” opening a file. What kind of problem is it?
items.correct: An access or permissions problem
items.explanation: Reaching the server proves connectivity; permission denied comes from file ownership or mode.

items.text: A shell script written on Windows fails on Linux with “bad interpreter”. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Linux server’s clock is set wrongly
The script is stored on an exFAT USB drive
Windows line endings in the script file
The user’s DNS suffix is not configured
items.correct: Windows line endings in the script file
items.explanation: CRLF line endings make the interpreter line invalid; save or convert the file with LF endings.

items.text: Why should technicians use their own named admin accounts?
options: So they never need to use MFA when signing in to servers
So their accounts never expire or lock out
So users can borrow them when they need rights
So every privileged change is traceable to a person
items.correct: So every privileged change is traceable to a person
items.explanation: Named accounts give accountability; shared admin accounts hide who made a change.

items.text: When is a Microsoft Defender Offline scan most useful?
options: When the PC has no internet connection at all
When the user wants a faster scan than a quick one
When the antivirus licence has recently expired
When malware may be hiding from the running Windows
items.correct: When malware may be hiding from the running Windows
items.explanation: The offline scan runs from the recovery environment before Windows loads, catching malware that hides while Windows runs.

items.text: BitLocker is suspended for a firmware update then the device is lost. What residual risk remains?
options: None — the drive stays fully protected
The recovery key is erased from AD
The key is unprotected while suspended
The TPM locks the drive permanently
items.correct: The key is unprotected while suspended
items.explanation: Suspending BitLocker stores the key unprotected on the disk, so the data is readable until protection is resumed.

items.text: Which log source best helps prove who changed a privileged GPO?
items.correct: Directory-service audit events
items.explanation: Directory-service auditing records who changed a Group Policy object and when.

items.text: Outlook fails; Word and the next desk work. What is the scope?
items.correct: One app on one PC
items.explanation: If only Outlook fails while Word on the same PC and the next desk both work, the scope is one app on one PC. That rules out a floor-wide incident and a power fault, and a reimage is far too big a change. See 11.1.

items.text: You started a PC in Safe Mode using msconfig. What must you do afterwards?
options: Untick Safe boot so it starts normally again
Turn off System Restore to save disk space
Run sfc /scannow before the next restart
Disable the network adapter for safety
items.correct: Untick Safe boot so it starts normally again
items.explanation: msconfig’s Safe boot persists until cleared; otherwise every restart returns to Safe Mode.

items.text: Which step must come first in a rebuild plan?
options: Download the newest drivers for the device model
Back up the user’s data and test the backup
Book a meeting room for the change review
Order a replacement drive in case it fails
items.correct: Back up the user’s data and test the backup
items.explanation: Data protection comes first; a backup is only trusted once a restore has been tested.

items.text: One process’s memory use climbs steadily for hours and never drops. What is the likely problem?
options: A DNS server that is too slow
A memory leak in that process
items.correct: A memory leak in that process
items.explanation: Steady growth without release is the signature of a leak in the growing process.

items.text: What is the purpose of a backout plan in a change request?
options: To list everyone who will be told about the change and when
To explain why the change is needed at all
To undo the change if it fails, at a stated trigger
To record who approved the change and when
items.correct: To undo the change if it fails, at a stated trigger
items.explanation: The backout plan gives tested steps to reverse the change and the condition for using them.

items.text: Password in the ticket to help the next guy?
options: Yes, if the ticket is private
items.correct: No
items.explanation: A password never goes in the ticket, even if the user agrees or the ticket is private: tickets are widely read and kept. The next technician uses the approved reset path. See 12.2.

items.text: Which recovery option is most appropriate when a single file was deleted from a volume with previous-day backups but the volume is healthy?
options: Restore the file from backup or Previous Versions
A full bare-metal recovery of the whole server
items.correct: Restore the file from backup or Previous Versions
items.explanation: Restore just the file from backup or Previous Versions; larger recoveries add risk and downtime.

items.text: Which item belongs in a knowledge-base article for a known fault?
options: The user’s password at the time of the fault
Screenshots that show the user’s personal files
The names of everyone who reported the fault
The steps to verify that the fix worked
items.correct: The steps to verify that the fix worked
items.explanation: A KB article includes verification and escalation steps; secrets and personal data never belong in it.

items.text: Chapter 13 pass bar?
options: You noted the password for the next tech
Labs submit and notes still meet the Block 1 bar
You ran diskpart clean to practise it
You left the firewall off to save time in the lab
items.correct: Labs submit and notes still meet the Block 1 bar
items.explanation: Chapter 13 is passed when the labs are submitted and the notes still meet the Block 1 standard: facts, tests and the next step. A recorded password, diskpart clean or a firewall left off fail it. See 13.6.

items.text: After removing a stale hosts-file entry, what is the best verification step?
options: Restart the PC and close the ticket at once
Run netsh winsock reset to make it stick
Flush the cache and resolve the name again
Ask the user to wait until tomorrow
items.correct: Flush the cache and resolve the name again
items.explanation: Flushing removes any cached wrong answer; resolving again proves the fix before the page is retested.

items.text: List processes:
items.correct: Before you reboot
items.explanation: List processes before you reboot, because a reboot clears the running processes you are trying to see (8.3: a reboot is a change). After a reboot the evidence is gone, and this applies on Windows too. See 13.6 / 8.3.

items.text: WMIC has been removed from current Windows 11. Which PowerShell command gives a summary of the IP address, gateway and DNS servers per adapter?
items.correct: Get-NetIPConfiguration
items.explanation: Microsoft removed the WMIC utility from Windows 11 24H2 and later (WMI itself remains). Get-NetIPConfiguration (NetTCPIP module) summarises addresses, gateway and DNS servers per adapter; the other cmdlets restart an adapter, clear the DNS cache, or list only the DNS server addresses per interface (Get-DnsClientServerAddress), not the addresses and gateway.

items.text: A /28 provides how many usable IPv4 hosts (standard host addressing)?
items.explanation: 2^4 = 16 addresses minus network and broadcast = 14.

items.text: Which port and transport does SNMP polling use by default?
items.correct: UDP 161
items.explanation: Agents listen on UDP 161; traps go to UDP 162. UDP 514 is syslog.

items.text: BPDU Guard is enabled on access ports to?
options: Shut down an edge port that receives STP BPDUs
Speed up STP convergence on the trunk links
items.correct: Shut down an edge port that receives STP BPDUs
items.explanation: BPDU Guard err-disables an edge port that receives STP BPDUs (someone attached a switch or made a loop).

items.text: A run of 400 m between two buildings needs 10 Gb/s. Which medium fits?
items.correct: Multimode or single-mode fibre
items.explanation: Copper Ethernet stops at 100 m; 10GBASE-SR (OM3/OM4 multimode) reaches about 300–400 m and single-mode goes further.

items.text: A dual-homed BGP edge loses one provider. Best outcome with proper design?
options: Traffic shifts to the remaining provider per routing policy
All sessions fail until the lost provider comes back
items.correct: Traffic shifts to the remaining provider per routing policy
items.explanation: With proper design, routes via the failed provider are withdrawn and traffic follows the remaining provider’s routes per policy.

items.text: A site-to-site VPN comes up but traffic does not pass interesting traffic selectors. Focus area?
options: The pre-shared key on both peers
The ISP circuit speed at each of the sites
The DHCP scope at the remote site
The traffic selectors and routes into the tunnel
items.correct: The traffic selectors and routes into the tunnel
items.explanation: The tunnel is up (authentication worked); traffic fails to match the selectors (crypto ACLs) or is not routed into the tunnel.

items.text: Which DNS record type maps a name to an IPv6 address?
items.correct: AAAA
items.explanation: AAAA records map names to IPv6 addresses; A records are IPv4.

items.text: A DMZ hosts public web servers. What is the design intent?
options: Separate Internet-facing services from internal networks
Speed up traffic to public servers
Host the domain controllers there for remote users
items.correct: Separate Internet-facing services from internal networks
items.explanation: A DMZ separates Internet-facing services from internal zones so a compromise there does not reach the internal network.

items.text: Syslog messages are critical for IR but are only stored on each device. Weakness?
options: Too much storage used on each device
Log messages arrive too late to use
Syslog cannot record a severity level
items.correct: No central, tamper-resistant log store
items.explanation: Logs kept only on each device cannot be correlated, may be lost on reboot and can be altered by an attacker; centralise them.

items.text: Control plane policing is intended to?
options: Limit how much bandwidth each user gets
Prioritise voice traffic across the WAN
Protect the device CPU from control-plane floods
Encrypt the management sessions to the device
items.correct: Protect the device CPU from control-plane floods
items.explanation: CoPP rate-limits traffic destined to the device CPU so floods cannot starve routing and management processes.

items.text: Guest Wi-Fi users should reach the Internet but nothing internal. Which design does that?
options: A separate guest VLAN/zone with a policy allowing only Internet
Putting guests on the staff VLAN, but with a different SSID name
items.correct: A separate guest VLAN/zone with a policy allowing only Internet
items.explanation: Segmentation plus a deny-internal policy enforces least privilege; SSID names and hiding do not.

items.text: Only users in one building cannot reach any server; other buildings are fine. Where do you look first?
options: The building’s shared uplink and gateway
Each affected user’s PC in turn, one by one
items.correct: The building’s shared uplink and gateway
items.explanation: Scope narrows the fault: what those users share and others do not is the likeliest place.

items.text: Why time-box each troubleshooting step during a major incident?
options: To avoid writing status updates while the team is busy fixing
To decide when to escalate or roll back instead of drifting
items.correct: To decide when to escalate or roll back instead of drifting
items.explanation: Time boxes force a decision point: escalate, roll back or try the next theory.

items.text: Which command assigns an access port to VLAN 30 in interface configuration mode?
items.correct: switchport access vlan 30
items.explanation: switchport access vlan sets an access port’s VLAN; the trunk command applies to trunks only.

items.text: Which output confirms the router has a connected route for its VLAN 10 subinterface?
options: The VLAN listed in show vlan brief
An ARP entry for the router’s own subinterface address
A “C” entry for the VLAN 10 subnet in show ip route
items.correct: A “C” entry for the VLAN 10 subnet in show ip route
items.explanation: Connected routes (code C) appear once the subinterface has an address and is up.
